subject: PII handling for prompts/outputs — follow-up and confirmation
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Oct 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: PII handling for prompts/outputs — follow-up and confirmation

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for taking time today — great conversation. Quick recap and an ask:

What we covered:
- BrightPath will pass short patient prompts (de-identified first pass) and occasional patient identifiers for lookup flows.
- You’re most concerned about where prompts/LLM outputs are stored, how long they are retained, and what logging/access controls exist for debugging and audits.

Next steps I promised: provide a concise confirmation of how Redwood handles prompts/outputs across our deployment modes (Hosted, Dedicated, Private) and what options BrightPath has for retention/config and redaction. Below is a short draft — can you confirm this aligns with your expectations or point out gaps?

Draft confirmation (high level):
- Hosted API: Prompt text and model outputs are encrypted at rest and in transit. By default, short-term request logs (prompts + outputs) are retained for 30 days for quality, abuse detection, and debugging. Logs are accessible to Redwood support on a need-to-know basis and are covered under our SOC 2 controls and DPA. Customers can opt out of logging for production requests under an enterprise DPA (or use our Dedicated/Private options).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): Logs and telemetry can be routed into a customer-managed VPC/S3 endpoint. Default retention is 90 days but is configurable; Redwood can also forward logs to your SIEM for long-term retention. Keys are customer-managed (KMS) if requested.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): All logs and artifacts remain inside your environment. Redwood control plane access can be restricted; no prompts/outputs are sent to Redwood-hosted storage unless explicitly enabled.
- Redaction & PII handling: We offer configurable server-side redaction rules and recommend client-side tokenization for sensitive fields. We can provide sample redaction rules and a short integration guide.

Attachments I’m including: SOC2 Type II summary and our standard DPA.

Can you confirm these cover your requirements or flag any compliance needs (e.g., specific retention windows, audit log export, or encryption/HSM requirements)? Once you confirm, Neha will provide a short, signed confirmation note for procurement and security review.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0123

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. That looks good overall — a few clarifications we need before we move to procurement:

1) For Hosted API: when you say "retained for 30 days," is that full prompt+output text or only metadata/trace? Are there any circumstances where older logs are archived beyond 30 days (backups, legal holds)?
2) For Dedicated: can you confirm the process for forwarding logs to our S3 and whether Redwood ever holds secondary copies outside our bucket?
3) For Private: do you have any recommended default retention configs you suggest (we need to propose a 1-year and 7-year retention model internally)?

Also our security team asked for confirmation that access to logs is auditable (who accessed, when) and that all logs are encrypted with customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private.

Would appreciate a short, formal confirmation we can attach to our vendor review.

Subject: RE: PII handling for prompts/outputs — follow-up and confirmation

Hi Jordan —

Thanks for the questions. Below is a short, formal confirmation you can attach to your vendor review. I’ve also attached our SOC2 summary and the DPA as Marissa mentioned.

Short confirmation (Redwood Inference) — prompts & outputs handling

1) Hosted API (Redwood-hosted):
- What is stored: By default, our hosted API captures full request and response payloads (prompts and model outputs) for troubleshooting, quality, and abuse detection.
- Retention: Default retention is 30 days for request/response content. We do not archive full request/response payloads beyond 30 days. Backups contain only encrypted system state and do not include customer PII-containing payloads.
- Access & audit: Access to request/response logs is limited to authorized staff and is logged in our audit system (who, when, reason). Support access is granted via documented procedures and requires approval for production data access.
- Opt-out/controls: Customers who require no logging for production traffic can either (a) enable a logging-opt-out flag in their account under an enterprise DPA, (b) use Dedicated (where logs go to customer-managed endpoints), or (c) use Private deployment.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity / VPC-connected):
- What is stored: Request/response logs can be configured to be delivered to a customer-managed S3 bucket or other customer endpoint inside their VPC.
- Retention & copies: Redwood will not retain secondary copies of request/response payloads outside of the customer-managed endpoint. Default Redwood-managed retention for telemetry is 90 days for performance metrics (not full payloads) unless otherwise agreed. If customers request Redwood to buffer logs temporarily for transit, that buffer is encrypted and retained only for the transit window (configurable, typically <24 hours).
- KMS/HSM: We support customer-managed KMS keys for encryption at rest for Dedicated deployments; HSM-backed key management can be discussed for enterprise agreements.
- Auditing: We provide access logs that show which Redwood service account pushed data and timestamps; customers can enable additional SIEM ingestion for full audit trails.

3) Private (customer-controlled VPC / on-prem):
- What is stored: All logs and request/response artifacts remain inside the customer environment. Redwood does not receive or store prompts/outputs in our hosted systems unless explicitly enabled by the customer.
- Retention: Retention is controlled by BrightPath; we can provide recommended retention templates (examples: 1 year for operational logs, 7 years for audit/legal retention) and accompanying retention policy text.
- KMS/HSM & audit: Full support for customer KMS and on-prem HSM; audit logs remain within customer systems.

4) Redaction & PII mitigation options:
- Server-side redaction rules: Redwood offers configurable redaction pipelines (regex, JSON path rules) to remove or mask PII before it is persisted.
- Client-side tokenization: We recommend tokenizing identifiers prior to sending when possible.
- Additional controls: We can run a short integration test to validate redaction rules against sample payloads.

Attachments included: Redwood_SOC2_Type2_2028.pdf; Redwood-DPA-v1.4.pdf; data-flow-diagram-brightpath.png

If you’d like, we can convert this into a signed one-page attestation for your vendor team (Neha, Security) — let me know and I’ll sign and return.

Best regards,
Neha Kapoor
